description: A typical application chain needs: biometrics enrolment, a consular interview, an approved-panel medical examination, and passport submission and collection - each a separate visit, each with its own scheduling system.
time_note: Elapsed across the chain, not working time.

description: Immigration medicals must be done by a specific approved doctor. Where no panel physician operates in Iran or the applicant's city, the medical itself becomes an international trip with an expiry date attached.
energy_note: A medical certificate that expires before the visa decides.

aspect: EXAMPLE - results expire out of sync
description: Police certificates, medicals and language tests all have validity windows, and a long security screening can outlast them - so documents must be obtained again, at full cost, purely because the decision took too long.
energy_note: Paying twice for the same clean record because the state was slow.

aspect: EXAMPLE - time off work nobody grants
description: Each trip is several days of leave. An employee in Iran explaining repeated absences for foreign embassy appointments is also disclosing an intention to emigrate, to an employer who may act on it.
energy_note: The process forces you to tell your boss you are leaving.

aspect: SCENARIO - the medical that expired first
description: Omid's immigration medical is done in March and is valid twelve months. Security screening runs nineteen. He is asked to repeat the medical: CAD 450, a new appointment six weeks out, and the same chest X-ray of the same healthy chest.
energy_note: Paying again to re-prove a fact that did not change.
